# personas/export

Everything in this folder except this README is generated by
[../export.py](../export.py) from the `../*.persona.md` source files.
**Never hand-edit a generated file.** Edit the persona source and
regenerate; a hand edit is overwritten on the next run and makes `--check`
fail until then.

Each generated Markdown file starts with a comment saying so:

```
<!-- GENERATED from personas/<id>.persona.md. DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY. -->
```

What a persona is and when to use each one: [../README.md](../README.md).
What each surface is for, in full: [../SURFACES.md](../SURFACES.md).

## What is here

| path | what it is | who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `claude-agents/<id>.md` | the persona as a Claude Code subagent: frontmatter plus a system prompt | Claude Code, after you copy it into a `.claude/agents/` folder |
| `claude-skills/<id>/SKILL.md` | the persona as a Claude Code skill you invoke by name | Claude Code, after you copy the `<id>/` folder into a `.claude/skills/` folder |
| `cards/<id>.md` | a readable one-pager | people, and the tutorials |
| `personas.json` | one JSON array with each persona's frontmatter (`id`, `name`, `family`, `one_liner`, `invoke_when`, `asks_for`, `refuses`, `produces`, `source_file`), no body | other tools: Codex, Cursor, the raw API |

The source files stay tool-neutral on purpose. Anything Claude-specific,
such as the agent's `model:` line, is added by the exporter, and
`tests/test_personas.py` fails if a source's frontmatter carries a
tool-specific field.

## No README inside claude-agents/ or claude-skills/

Do not add one. People copy those two folders straight into `.claude/`.
There, every `.md` file in the agents folder is read as an agent
definition, so a README becomes a broken agent, and the skills folder is
meant to hold nothing but one folder per skill. This file sits one level up
for that reason.

## Regenerate and check

From the repo root, with Python 3.12+:

```bash
python personas/export.py           # rewrite every generated file
python personas/export.py --check   # exit 0 if current, 1 if not
```

`--check` regenerates into a temporary directory and compares each file it
produced with the one here, stopping at the first missing or out-of-sync
file. `tests/test_personas.py` runs it, so stale exports fail the suite.
Commit the source and the regenerated exports together.

Three things `--check` does not catch:

- **Files it does not generate.** This README is ignored, which is why it
  is safe here. So is a leftover export: deleting or renaming a persona
  source leaves its old files behind. Remove them yourself.
- **Line endings.** It compares in text mode, so CRLF looks the same as LF.
  `test_everything_is_lf` in `tests/test_personas.py` catches that instead.
  The exporter writes with `encoding="utf-8"` and `newline="\n"`; keep it
  that way.
- **Whether the content is right.** It proves the exports match the
  sources, not that the sources say something sensible.
